title: A completed no-removal migration clears its record, so a later --remove-backlog run still collides
description:
Filed from the LCLI-699 round-2 review (F1). LCLI-699 makes a rerun after an APPLIED migration idempotent ONLY while the pending record `.lore/quest-backlog-migration.pending.json` survives. A migration that COMPLETES with no removal requested clears its record (clearPendingQuestMigration runs on the success path, init.ts:574), so a later run still re-enters the fresh path and collides.

REPRO (reachable by following the tool own stderr notice): (1) `lore init --tracker quest --migrate-backlog` (no removal flag) writes the record, applies the migration, resolveScriptedBacklogRemoval returns removed:false and prints "Pass --remove-backlog to delete them", then the record is cleared; exit 0. (2) The operator follows that notice: `lore init --tracker quest --migrate-backlog --remove-backlog` -- store.read is undefined -> fresh path -> preview -> write -> apply, and Quest meets the aliases the first run created -> type=conflict, exit 5.

The LCLI-699 ACs are scoped to "a rerun holding a pending migration record", so the code is compliant; this is the residual path the CHANGELOG headline is now scoped away from.

DESIGN QUESTION (opum-doc): should a completed migration KEEP its record when no removal was requested, so a later --remove-backlog run resumes it (and how would that interact with a genuinely NEW migration of the same backlog); or should removal be status-first, asking Quest whether the digest is already applied rather than relying on the local record? UNSTAMPED -- no assignee, no ACs; opum-doc decides.
